## Context

Today `rebar bridge` exposes `{preview,sync,pause,resume}`. No `bridge status` subcommand exists, and the earlier top-level `bridge-status` command was fully removed. This story creates the canonical `rebar bridge status` command over durable state and re-introduces `rebar bridge-status` as a compatibility alias. Both spellings use the same parser and core so options, text and JSON schemas, messages, state reads, and exit codes stay identical. Existing preview, sync, pause, and resume behavior remains unchanged.

The current production canary queries GitHub Actions for heartbeat state. Reconciler health also has two overlapping producers: `health.record_pass` and `pass_io._write_pass_record`. The per-pass `bridge_state/health/<pass_id>.json` files live in an ignored ephemeral directory and are not durable. The tickets branch is durable, but the workflow commit-back step at lines 309-310 is gated by `if: steps.reconcile.outputs.paused != true` and is skipped after a reconcile step exits nonzero because it lacks `always()`. Therefore commit-back cannot be the witness for a hard failure.

## Durable state and writer contract

Consolidate the two pass-record producers into one. A mutating reconciler pass writes minimal JSON truth to the Git object named by `refs/reconciler/last-pass` from a process-level finalization path that runs for both success and process-surviving hard failure. The record contains schema version, pass id, selected environment id, outcome, failure kind when present, completion timestamp, and the lock fence observed for the pass. The ref is authoritative.

Update the ref with observed-OID compare-and-swap using `--force-with-lease=refs/reconciler/last-pass:<observed-oid>`. Retry boundedly with backoff after refetch on contention. Exhausted contention or a persistent push/network/permission failure is an operational failure: emit a clear error and nonzero process result, and never claim that the pass was durably recorded.

Rich detail is one fixed rolling file, `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/last-pass.json`, overwritten rather than accumulated per pass and committed through the normal tickets-branch path when that path runs. Status uses detail only when its pass id and environment id match the authoritative ref record. Missing, stale, or mismatched rich detail is reported as `detail_status` and omitted from the detail payload; it never replaces or changes the authoritative verdict.

Remove the duplicate health producers plus dead `pre_fsck`, `post_fsck`, and `capture_baseline` data. Update every caller and assertion in `health.py`, `pass_io.py`, `reconcile.py`, `applier.py`, health/schema/baseline/wiring tests, invariant/filter tests, store compatibility, and scratch-exclusion tests. After claim, perform semantic reference lookup plus an `rg` sweep for `_write_pass_record`, `record_pass`, `capture_baseline`, `pre_fsck`, and `post_fsck` before removal.

## Environment identity

An explicit `REBAR_ENV_ID` always wins. The reconcile workflow continues explicitly supplying `${{ vars.REBAR_ENV_ID || reconciler }}`, preserving current CI behavior. Outside that workflow, an unset id becomes stable `local:<repo-env-id>` derived from the checkout `.env-id`; it must never default to `reconciler`. The writer stamps the selected id. Status accepts an explicit target environment option, and the canary explicitly requests `reconciler`, so a developer pass is returned as `FOREIGN` rather than production state.

## Status snapshot and exact contract

`bridge status` is a fast, read-only, non-mutating single snapshot. Add its parser, metavar, help, and dispatch in `_bridge_commands.py` and route the top-level compatibility alias through the identical argument parser/core. Status never calls `steal()` and never sleeps for a lease. It reads the authoritative last-pass ref, optional matching rich detail, pause state, and the lock ref OID/fence/lease metadata.

Text and structured output expose the same verdict and facts. Exact verdict and exit contract:

- `HEALTHY`, matching successful last-pass record, exit 0.
- `PAUSED`, matching state while intentionally paused, exit 0 even when old; pause takes precedence over age failure.
- `RUNNING`, lock currently held in this single snapshot, exit 0 and include lock OID, fence, and lease.
- `STALE`, matching non-paused record older than an explicitly supplied `--max-age`, exit 1.
- Omitting `--max-age` disables age failure; there is no implicit threshold.
- `FOREIGN`, durable record environment differs from the explicitly selected target, exit 1 with both ids.
- `NEVER_RUN`, no durable last-pass record and no live lock, exit 1. The compatibility spelling preserves the former missing-status failure class and exit 1 while using the new shared schema/message.
- `FAILED`, last-pass records a process-surviving hard failure, exit 1 with `failure_kind`.
- `CRASHED` is not inferred by one status invocation. It is the canary result when two read-only snapshots separated by one configured lease show the same lock OID and fence; exit 1 in the canary/escalation path.

The two witnesses are deliberately separate. Last-pass records success and failures for which the process can execute finalization. SIGKILL, OOM, or runner teardown cannot update last-pass; only a non-advancing lock fence across one lease witnesses that crash. The scheduled canary takes two status snapshots separated by one lease and classifies advancing fence as `RUNNING` and unchanged OID/fence as `CRASHED`. It does not compare wall-clock heartbeat timestamps.

## Canary cutover and rollback

Production defaults the canary heartbeat source to canonical `bridge status`. The canary workflow first fetches `+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*`, explicitly targets environment `reconciler`, takes the two snapshots when a lock is present, and keeps the existing ticket escalation/dedup tags and failure behavior. The canonical source performs no GitHub Actions heartbeat API query.

For one release, retain the GitHub Actions API heartbeat source behind explicit rollback selection `REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE=github-api`; default is `status`. Tests cover both selections. Removing that rollback option is out of scope and will be separately tracked after the compatibility window.

## Verification plan

Author all behavioral tests RED-first under held-out TDD. The happy path proves a matching durable success. Held-out edge and E2E tests prove:

- canonical and legacy command parity for options, text/JSON, schema, errors, exits, and no mutation;
- `HEALTHY`, `PAUSED`, `RUNNING`, `STALE`, `FOREIGN`, `NEVER_RUN`, `FAILED`, and canary `CRASHED` contracts;
- omitted `--max-age` disables age failure and paused remains exit 0;
- local unset identity cannot masquerade as `reconciler`, while explicit CI/default workflow identity remains unchanged;
- hard process-surviving failure still pushes the minimal durable ref when workflow commit-back is skipped;
- SIGKILL/OOM is represented only by stalled fence and the two-snapshot lease classification;
- last-pass CAS contention retries and persistent ref push failure fails loudly;
- fixed rich detail mismatch/missing behavior and absence of unbounded per-pass files;
- canary fetches reconciler refs, consumes canonical status, preserves ticket escalation, defaults away from heartbeat API queries, and still supports the explicit GitHub API rollback source;
- all old bridge preview/sync/pause/resume consumers and behavior remain green.

Proving commands are the focused status, reconciler health, lock, canary, workflow-wiring, help, and compatibility suites, followed by `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` from the worktree virtualenv.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New `bridge status` and re-introduced `bridge-status` are identical read-only entrypoints while preview/sync/pause/resume remain compatible.
- [ ] The exact structured verdict and exit contracts above are implemented, including never-run, foreign, omitted max-age, paused, hard failure, and held lock.
- [ ] Local and CI environment identities cannot collide; existing workflow default `reconciler` is preserved.
- [ ] One consolidated producer records success and process-surviving failure to the authoritative last-pass ref with CAS, bounded retry, and loud persistent-push failure.
- [ ] Rich detail uses one fixed rolling file and safely degrades when missing or mismatched.
- [ ] Crash detection uses two read-only fence snapshots across one lease; status never mutates or blocks for a lease.
- [ ] The canary fetches reconciler refs, defaults to canonical status without a heartbeat API query, preserves ticket escalation, and offers the one-release rollback source.
- [ ] RED-first focused tests plus full lint, typecheck, and test gates prove the contracts and compatibility.
